Item 12 is sex-specific, so two versions of the scale were created and presented to women and men, respectively. section_summary.evidence_source: Body Appreciation Scale (BAS; Avalos et al., 2005). Item 12 of the scale, which refers to the impact of media images, is sex-specific (Tylka, personal communication, 2007; refers to unrealistically thin images for women and unrealistically muscular images for men), and so two versions of the scale were created and presented to women and men, respectively. All items were rated on a 5-point scale (1 = never, 2= seldom, 3= sometimes, 4= often, 5 = always), with higher scores reflecting greater body appreciation. Responses on all 13 items were averaged to obtain an overall body appreciation score.

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS; Avalos et al., 2005), a 13-item self-report measure (items averaged) with a sex-specific item 12 and 5-point response scale. It notes the English version's unidimensional structure for women, 3-week test-retest reliability, and evidence of construct, discriminant, and incremental validity. No sample characteristics, BMI assessment, or correlations with BMI are reported in this section, and no studies are labeled (e.g., 'Study 1').
section_summary.evidence_source: "Body Appreciation Scale (BAS; Avalos et al., 2005) This is a 13-item scale developed to measure four aspects of positive body image... Item 12 of the scale... All items were rated on a 5-point scale... Responses on all 13 items were averaged to obtain an overall body appreciation score. The English version of the scale showed a unidimensional structure for women, remained reliable after a 3-week interval, and showed good construct, discriminant and incremental validities (Avalos et al., 2005)."
